v3.lede: Cloudy, yellowed headlights restored back to clear, plus protection film and legal-depth smoke for headlights and taillights. Most vehicles are done the same day.

prices.lede: How hazed the lenses are, how many lights, and whether film goes on afterward set the price.

blocks.heading: Clear lenses again.
paragraphs: Headlight lenses are plastic, not glass. The Nevada sun breaks down the factory coating on that plastic, and once it goes the lens turns cloudy, yellow and rough. It is not dirt, so washing does nothing.
Restoration removes the damaged surface layer and seals the fresh surface, which brings the lens back to clear and puts more of your headlight output back on the road at night.

blocks.heading: Film over the lens.
paragraphs: Protection film is a clear urethane layer over the lens that takes the sun, the rock chips and the sand instead of the lens. It is the same family of film as the clear bra we install on paint, available for headlights, taillights or both.
The best time to add it is right after a restoration, or on a new vehicle before the sun has had a chance to start on it.

blocks.heading: Legal-depth smoke.
paragraphs: We tint headlights and taillights for a darker, more finished look. How dark is not a fixed number: it depends on your housings and how much light they put out to begin with, so we look at your actual lights rather than quoting a percentage off a chart.

blocks.heading: What Nevada requires.
blocks.lede: Two provisions worth knowing, quoted from the statute rather than from a forum.

items.detail: A tail lamp must emit a red light plainly visible from a distance of 500 feet to the rear.
Rear lamps, reflectors and marker lamps near the rear must display or reflect red, and front marker lamps amber. A stop light may be red, amber or yellow.

blocks.note: Nevada sets these as requirements about what your lights do, not as a percentage for how dark a film may be. For window tint rules, see Nevada tint law.

items.question: Can cloudy or yellowed headlights be fixed, or do I need new ones?
items.answer: In most cases they can be restored, for a fraction of the cost of new housings. Restoration removes the damaged surface layer, then a protective clear layer goes over the fresh surface. For longer protection we can apply clear film over the lenses instead.

items.question: How long does headlight restoration take?
items.answer: Most vehicles are done the same day. If you want protection film over the lenses afterward, that is best done at the same visit.

items.question: Can you tint or smoke my headlights and taillights?
items.answer: Yes, in legal-depth smoke. How dark depends on your housings and how much light they put out, so we look at your vehicle rather than quoting a percentage. Nevada requires a tail lamp to emit a red light plainly visible from 500 feet to the rear.
